title: Entergy supports student innovation at Red Stick Rumble
summary: Entergy served as title sponsor of the 13th annual Red Stick Rumble, held September 19 at Denham Springs High School. Entergy employees volunteered and served as judges, supporting student robotics teams from Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. Source

title: Natchez journeyman lineman to be honored at New Orleans Saints game
summary: Some linemen follow in the footsteps of their family members or family friends in choosing the profession. This was not the case for Corvan Day. He is a first-generation lineman who took an interest in becoming a lineman and found he has a passion for it. This passion shows through in the way he shows up every day as a journeyman lineman in Natchez and has earned him recognition as a Lineman of the Game. Source

title: Study finds a better way to separate zirconium and hafnium
summary: Different shapes of the crystals in the precipitates. (Image: OSU) Researchers at Oregon State University have published a paper in the Journal of the American Chemical Society on a new method of separating zirconium and hafnium, both of which are important for nuclear energy, and which are generally quite challenging to separate due to the elements’ similarities. According to the paper, more than 90 percent of Zr and Hf derived from zirconium silicate (zircon) is utilized by the nuclear industry, with high-purity Zr being widely used for nuclear fuel rod cladding. High-purity Hf is also used in the nuclear applications, typically for specialized control rods, such as those in nuclear submarines.

Up next: 2026 ANS Winter Conference & Expo
summary: Fall may have officially kicked off only last week, but the American Nuclear Society’s 2026 Winter Conference & Expo is already just around the corner. This year’s Winter Conference will be held November 15–18 at the Arizona Grand Resort & Spa in Phoenix. Registration is currently open, with early-bird pricing ending October 22. More details are available on the ANS website.

title: IAEA, Inter-American Development Bank expand nuclear cooperation
summary: In Latin America, only Argentina, Brazil, and Mexico currently have operating nuclear power plants. Less than 2 percent of the region’s electricity is generated by nuclear energy, in contrast to the roughly 8 percent of electricity generation from nuclear energy globally. These statistics, however, are expected to change, with nuclear deployments set to increase substantially in Latin America in the coming decades.
